name: InhibiZone
registry: Voluntary manufacturer patient information form database
question: Do rifampin- and minocycline-impregnated inflatable penile prostheses reduce first revision for infection compared with nonimpregnated prostheses?

arms.label: Minocycline- and rifampin-impregnated (InhibiZone) inflatable penile prosthesis

design.population: Men who received a first inflatable penile prosthesis between May 1, 2001 and December 31, 2008 and had a patient information form filed with the manufacturer.
design.description: Retrospective cohort from a voluntary manufacturer registry

verdictNote: Lower infection-related revision with impregnated implants in a voluntary manufacturer registry; implants were not randomized.
takeaway: In a retrospective analysis of voluntarily filed manufacturer forms for 39,005 first inflatable penile prostheses, minocycline- and rifampin-impregnated implants had initial revision for infection in 1.1% of 35,737 men versus 2.5% of 3,268 with nonimpregnated implants at up to 7.7 years.

reports.label: Up to 7.7-year revision analysis
reports.citation: Carson CC III, Mulcahy JJ, Harsch MR. Long-term infection outcomes after original antibiotic impregnated inflatable penile prosthesis implants: up to 7.7 years of followup. *J Urol.* 2011;185(2):614-618. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2010.09.094

results.measure: Initial revision due to infection at up to 7.7 years
results.note: Life-table survival analysis; P is the log-rank test.

delivery.label: Data source and enrollment window
delivery.value: Patient information forms voluntarily filed with the manufacturer after initial implantation; implants from May 1, 2001 to December 31, 2008.

delivery.label: Cohort size
delivery.value: More than 39,000 initial inflatable penile prostheses (35,737 impregnated; 3,268 nonimpregnated).

reports.label: Diabetic men, 7-year outcomes
reports.citation: Mulcahy JJ, Carson CC III. Long-term infection rates in diabetic patients implanted with antibiotic-impregnated versus nonimpregnated inflatable penile prostheses: 7-year outcomes. *Eur Urol.* 2011;60(1):167-172. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2011.01.046

results.measure: Initial revision due to infection at any time during the study period
results.note: Diabetic men with a first three-piece inflatable penile prosthesis implanted from 2001 to 2008.

results.measure: Life-table rate of infection-related revision at 7 years

harms.label: Infection-related revision at 7 years, diabetic versus nondiabetic men
harms.note: Diabetic men had a higher 7-year rate of revision for infection (1.88%) than men without diabetes (1.53%; log-rank P = 0.0052).

delivery.label: Device
delivery.value: Three-piece inflatable penile prostheses in all men.

reports.label: Replacement implants
reports.citation: Nehra A, Carson CC III, Chapin AK, Ginkel AM. Long-term infection outcomes of 3-piece antibiotic impregnated penile prostheses used in replacement implant surgery. *J Urol.* 2012;188(3):899-903. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2012.04.116

results.measure: Secondary revision due to infection at up to 6.6 years

delivery.label: Data source and population
delivery.value: Patient information forms voluntarily submitted to the manufacturer after replacement implantation from 2001 to 2007; only men whose first recorded operation replaced a previously implanted prosthesis.
